mainTopic: How a שומר can use a תנאי to change his Torah obligations, the rules for a valid תנאי, and the start of פרק השואל את הפרה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the case of a shepherd who bragged to a thief about his men, dogs and slings and was then robbed. Bragging like this counts as leading the flock into a dangerous place, so the loss is his fault. A new משנה then teaches that each kind of שומר may make a condition freeing himself from a שבועה or from paying. It also gives general rules: a condition against the Torah is void, a condition said after the action is void, and a condition said first that can be fulfilled is valid. The גמרא asks how a שומר's condition can work if it goes against the Torah. It first says the משנה follows רבי יהודה. Then it settles on רבי מאיר: the שומר never took on the Torah's duties in the first place. A ברייתא adds that a שומר שכר can take on a שואל's liability, and שמואל and רבי יוחנן argue about whether a קנין is needed for this. Next, the גמרא shows that the rule about conditions that can be fulfilled is רבי יהודה בן תימא's view, and the הלכה follows him: an impossible condition is ignored. The chapter then closes, and a new chapter opens with the rule that a borrower whose owner is working with him does not pay.

steps.title: The shepherd who boasted about his protection
steps.stepSummary: The question ends: a shepherd boasted to a thief about his men, dogs and slings, and the thief then stole from him. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: The shepherd said: 'We have so many men with us, so many dogs with us, and so many slings ready for us.' Then the thief went and took an animal from him. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question about a shepherd who taunted a thief by bragging that his flock was well protected, and then got robbed. It asks whether the shepherd is responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being robbed by force is normally an אונס, something a shepherd cannot prevent. The question is whether his bragging provoked the thief. If it did, the loss is partly his own fault.

phrases.english: Such and such men are with us,
phrases.notes: This is the shepherd talking, bragging to the thief so he won't dare attack.

phrases.english: such and such dogs are with us,
such and such slings are ready for us.
And the thief went and took from him. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲזַל וּשְׁקַל מִינֵּיהּ, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a question that began before this section, about a shepherd's liability for theft.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a shepherd liable when his own boasting provoked the thief who robbed him?

steps.title: Boasting is like leading the flock into danger
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the shepherd is treated as if he took the animals to a place full of wild beasts and bandits.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is as if he led them to a place of packs of wild animals and bandits.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is given. By bragging, the shepherd brought the danger on himself, so it is as if he walked the flock into a dangerous place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shepherd who leads animals into danger is careless, and he cannot claim the loss was an אונס. Taunting the thief created the risk, so the robbery counts as his fault.
steps.whatToRemember: A שומר who causes the danger himself, even just by provoking a thief with words, cannot claim the loss was an unavoidable אונס.

phrases.english: He said to him:
It is as if he led them to a place
of packs of wild animals and bandits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הֲרֵי הוֹלִיכָן לִמְקוֹם גְּדוּדֵי חַיָּה וְלִסְטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shepherd is liable, because boasting is like bringing the flock into a dangerous place.

steps.title: Bailees may stipulate their way out of obligations
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that each type of שומר may make a condition freeing himself from his oath or payment. It also states that a condition against what is written in the Torah is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: An unpaid watchman may stipulate that he is exempt from an oath. A borrower may stipulate that he is exempt from paying. A paid watchman and a renter may stipulate that they are exempt from an oath and from paying. Anyone who stipulates against what is written in the Torah, his condition is void.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says each שומר can agree with the owner in advance to be freed from his usual Torah obligations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each שומר is freed from his own typical duty. A שומר חנם normally only swears, so he can drop the שבועה. A שואל normally pays, so he can drop the payment. A שומר שכר and a שוכר can drop both. In the same breath, the משנה says a condition against the Torah is void, and this sets up the גמרא's question.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה says the שומרים' conditions work, and right after that it says conditions against the Torah are void. That looks like a contradiction, and it is exactly what the גמרא asks about next.

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֶה שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם לִהְיוֹת פָּטוּר מִשְּׁבוּעָה,
phrases.english: An unpaid watchman may stipulate to be exempt from an oath,
and the borrower to be exempt from paying,
a paid watchman and the renter
to be exempt from an oath and from paying.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה –
phrases.english: Anyone who stipulates against what is written in the Torah –
his condition is void,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֶה שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם לִהְיוֹת פָּטוּר מִשְּׁבוּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each שומר may stipulate to be free of his usual oath or payment, but any condition against what is written in the Torah is void.

steps.title: When a condition works and when it fails
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds two more rules. A condition that comes after the action is void. A condition stated first, which can be fulfilled, is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any condition that has an action at its beginning, the condition is void. Any condition that he can fulfill in the end, and he stipulated with him from the beginning, his condition is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with general rules about how a condition must be built in order to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Order matters. If the action is said first and the condition only afterward, the condition does not take hold. If the condition is said first and it is something that can actually be fulfilled, it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An action at its beginning (the action is said before the condition)

steps.whatToRemember: A condition works only if it is not against the Torah, comes before the action, and can actually be fulfilled.

phrases.english: And any condition that has an action at its beginning –
phrases.notes: This means the person said the action first and only then added the condition.

phrases.english: his condition is void.
And any condition that he is able to fulfill in the end,
and he stipulated with him from the beginning –
his condition is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל תְּנַאי שֶׁיֵּשׁ מַעֲשֶׂה בִּתְחִילָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with more general rules about conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition placed after the action is void. A condition stated first that can be fulfilled is valid.

steps.title: Isn't the bailee's condition against the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a שומר's condition works, since the Torah itself set his oath and payment duties.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? He is stipulating against what is written in the Torah, and anyone who stipulates against what is written in the Torah, his condition is void!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first part of the משנה, using the משנה's own rule about conditions against the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah decides which שומר swears and which one pays. A condition that removes those duties looks like going against the Torah, which the same משנה says is void. So how can the שומרים' conditions work?

keyTerms.meaning: What is written in the Torah

phrases.english: Gemara:
Why?

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא,
phrases.english: He is stipulating against what is written in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: and anyone who stipulates against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? מַתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first ruling of the משנה using the משנה's own rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that שומרים may stipulate their way out of an oath or payment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These duties are set by the Torah, and a condition against the Torah is void, so the שומרים' conditions should not work.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, who says a condition about money matters is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה, who says that in a money matter, his condition stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 5 by naming an author for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר's duties of oath and payment are only about money. רבי יהודה holds that a person may make a condition against the Torah when it is a money matter. So a שומר's condition works.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is this?
It is Rabbi Yehuda,
who says: in a money matter,
his condition stands.
phrases.notes: He means even a condition that goes against what the Torah says.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי – רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5 by assigning the משנה to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A condition against the Torah's rules for a שומר should be void.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, a condition about money is valid even against the Torah.

steps.title: The ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה allows a condition against the Torah in money matters, while רבי מאיר does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man betroths a woman on condition that she has no claim to food, clothing or marital relations from him. רבי מאיר says she is betrothed and the condition is void. רבי יהודה says that in money matters the condition stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי יהודה really holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food and clothing are money matters, so רבי יהודה lets the husband give them up by a condition. רבי מאיר voids any condition against the Torah, even about money.

keyTerms.meaning: Food, clothing and marital relations, which a husband owes his wife

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
One who says to a woman:
"You are hereby betrothed to me
on condition that you have no claim on me
for food, clothing and marital relations"
she is betrothed, and his condition is void;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: in a money matter,
phrases.notes: Food and clothing are the money part. Marital relations are not.

phrases.english: his condition stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the view of רבי יהודה cited in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה allows a condition against the Torah in money matters
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about betrothal on condition of no food, clothing or marital relations

steps.title: A later clause sounds like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: the משנה later says any condition against the Torah is void, which is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say the משנה is רבי יהודה? Look at the later clause: anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah, his condition is void. That is רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 6 using another line from the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later clause voids every condition against the Torah and makes no exception for money matters. That matches רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really set it as (this view)?
The later clause of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: But can you set it as Rabbi Yehuda's view?
Say the later clause:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה –
phrases.english: Anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void.
We have arrived at Rabbi Meir!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The later clause voids all conditions against the Torah, which is רבי מאיר's view.

steps.title: The later clause is about non-money matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is still רבי יהודה, and the later clause speaks only about matters that are not money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is no problem. The משנה really is רבי יהודה, and the later clause is talking about something that is not money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה also agrees that a condition against the Torah is void in non-money matters, like marital relations. So the later clause fits him too.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (we keep our first answer)
A matter that is not about money

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
Really, it is Rabbi Yehuda,
and the later clause is about a matter that is not money.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the clause to a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The later clause voids every condition against the Torah, as רבי מאיר holds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The later clause speaks only about non-money matters, where רבי יהודה agrees.

steps.title: Another clause fits only רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises another clause: a condition that comes after the action is void. Only רבי מאיר holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the later clause: any condition that has the action at its start is void. Who do we know holds this idea? רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge against the idea that the משנה is רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the clause has nothing to do with money, so the answer of Step 9 cannot help. The rule that a condition after the action is void is known only from רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: The action comes first, before the condition
Whom have you heard (who holds this)?

phrases.english: Say the later clause:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל תְּנַאי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה בִּתְחִילָּתוֹ –
phrases.english: Any condition that has the action at its start,
phrases.notes: This is the rule from Step 4: the condition was said only after the action.

phrases.english: the condition is void.
Whom have you heard
who holds this idea?
Rabbi Meir,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: כׇּל תְּנַאי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה בִּתְחִילָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge after Step 9 answered the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that a condition after the action is void is held only by רבי מאיר, and it is not a money issue.

steps.title: Source that רבי מאיר holds the condition must come first
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר: a condition before the action counts, but a condition after the action does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught: אבא חלפתא of the village of Chananya said in the name of רבי מאיר: a condition before the action is a condition; an action before the condition is not a condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that this rule about timing is רבי מאיר's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא ties the timing rule of the משנה to רבי מאיר. That makes it hard to say the משנה is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Abba Chalafta, a man of the village of Chananya,
said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
If the condition comes before the action,
this is a valid condition;
if the action comes before the condition,
it is not a valid condition.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא חֲלַפְתָּא אִישׁ כְּפַר חֲנַנְיָא אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in Step 10 that this rule belongs to רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds a condition after the action is void
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of אבא חלפתא in the name of רבי מאיר

steps.title: The whole משנה is רבי מאיר, and the שומר never took on the duty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the רבי יהודה answer. The whole משנה is רבי מאיר, and the שומר's condition works because he never agreed to the Torah's duties in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the whole משנה is רבי מאיר. Here it is different, because from the start he never bound himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new, final answer to the question of Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שומר is not canceling a Torah law. The Torah's duties apply only to someone who agrees to be a שומר, and he made clear from the start that he was not taking them on. So even רבי מאיר agrees the condition works.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not bind himself (to the duty)

steps.whatToRemember: A שומר's condition is not a condition against the Torah. The Torah's duties never started, because he never agreed to take them on.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר still holds that conditions against the Torah are void. The point is that the שומר's case is not really such a condition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a שומר's duties come from his own agreement, so he can decide in advance how much he takes on.

phrases.english: Rather, the whole משנה is Rabbi Meir,
and here it is different,
because from the start he did not bind himself.
phrases.notes: He never agreed to the Torah's duties of a שומר, so there is nothing to cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כּוּלַּהּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the רבי יהודה approach after Steps 10–11 and gives a new answer to Step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reasoning that changes how the case is understood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שומר's condition works only because the משנה follows רבי יהודה's money-matter rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is רבי מאיר. The condition works because the שומר never took on the Torah's duties.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A שומר's advance condition is valid even according to רבי מאיר, since he never bound himself.

steps.title: A paid watchman can take on the liability of a borrower
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a שומר שכר can make a condition to be liable like a שואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: A paid watchman can make a condition to be like a borrower.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It teaches the opposite direction of the משנה: a שומר can make himself more liable, not only less liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that a שומר can make a condition to lower his liability. This ברייתא adds that a שומר שכר can also raise his liability to the level of a שואל, who must pay even for an אונס (an accident he could not prevent).

keyTerms.meaning: A borrower, who must pay even for accidents

phrases.english: It was taught: And a paid watchman can make a condition
to be like a borrower.
phrases.notes: He means taking on all of a borrower's liability, even for accidents.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: וּמַתְנֶה שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר לִהְיוֹת כְּשׁוֹאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing that a שומר's conditions work, the גמרא brings a ברייתא showing such a condition can also increase his liability.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר שכר may stipulate to carry the full liability of a שואל.

steps.title: How do mere words obligate him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this extra obligation takes effect, since it seems to be only spoken words.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does he take this on? With words alone?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the שומר becomes obligated. It is setting up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, just saying "I will pay" does not create a binding money obligation. So the גמרא wonders what makes this promise binding.

phrases.english: With what? With words?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי? בִּדְבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the mechanism behind the ברייתא in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What legal act makes the שומר שכר's added obligation binding?

steps.title: שמואל: a formal act of acquisition was done
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the ברייתא speaks of a case where a קנין was done.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is a case where they did a קנין with him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The obligation works because a formal קנין was done, not because of words alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנין is a formal act that makes a commitment binding. With a קנין, the promise to be like a שואל becomes a real obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a קנין with him (a formal binding act)

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Where they made an acquisition from him.
phrases.notes: Usually this means the שומר took hold of an item, like a cloth, to seal his promise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: בְּשֶׁקָּנוּ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 by narrowing the case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא speaks of a case where a קנין was made.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: his good reputation makes words enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says no קנין is needed, because the שומר gains a reputation as trustworthy and so truly commits himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it is where they did not make a קנין. Because of the benefit he gets from people saying he is a trustworthy man, he fully decides to obligate himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. Words alone are enough here, because the שומר gets something real in return: a good name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The benefit of being known as reliable is worth something to the שומר. Because he gains that, he sincerely commits himself, so no formal קנין is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: He fully decides and obligates himself

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל needs a קנין for a שומר to take on extra liability. רבי יוחנן says words are enough, because the good reputation he gains makes him truly commit.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say where they did not make an acquisition from him,
with that benefit
that a report goes out about him
that he is a trustworthy man –
he fully decides and obligates himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּשֶׁלֹּא קָנוּ מִיָּדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to step 14 that disagrees with שמואל's need for a קנין.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even without a קנין, the benefit of a trustworthy reputation makes the שומר truly commit himself.

steps.title: Whose view is the rule about conditions that can be fulfilled?
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's rule that a condition counts if it can be fulfilled, רב טבלא in the name of רב says this is רבי יהודה בן תימא's view, while the חכמים say even an impossible condition counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "Any condition that can be fulfilled in the end, etc." רב טבלא said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי יהודה בן תימא. But the חכמים say: Even if it cannot be fulfilled in the end, if he made the condition at the start, his condition stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. רב טבלא says the משנה follows one תנא, and the חכמים disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה's wording, a condition that can never be fulfilled seems not to count. רב טבלא says that is only רבי יהודה בן תימא's view. The חכמים say an impossible condition still counts, so the deal only works if it is fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: To fulfill it in the end

steps.confusionAlert: "His condition stands" does not mean the impossible thing happens. It means the condition is taken seriously, so the deal depends on it.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְקַיְּימוֹ בְּסוֹפוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: "And any [condition] that he can fulfill in the end, etc."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה. It goes on: if he made the condition at the start, it stands.

phrases.english: Rav Tavla said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא.
phrases.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima.
But the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְקַיְּימוֹ בְּסוֹפוֹ
phrases.english: Even though he cannot fulfill it in the end
and he made the condition about it at the start –
his condition stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְקַיְּימוֹ בְּסוֹפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's list of condition rules and explains the last clause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא. The חכמים hold that even an impossible condition is valid.

steps.title: A גט with impossible conditions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows the חכמים's view: a גט given on an impossible condition works only if the condition happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: "Here is your גט on condition that you go up to the sky, or go down to the depths, or swallow a reed one hundred אמות long, or cross the Great Sea on foot." If the condition happened, it is a גט. If the condition did not happen, it is not a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the חכמים's view. Even with impossible conditions, the גט depends on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These conditions can never really happen, yet the ברייתא still makes the גט depend on them. So in practice she is not divorced. This shows an impossible condition is not ignored, just as the חכמים said.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, an impossible condition is still a real condition. A גט given on such a condition does not take effect unless the condition happens.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "Here is your bill of divorce
on condition that you go up to the sky,
on condition that you go down to the depths,

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּבְלְעִי קָנֶה שֶׁל מֵאָה אַמָּה,
phrases.english: on condition that you swallow a reed of one hundred cubits,

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּעַבְרִי אֶת הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל בְּרַגְלַיִךְ״,
phrases.english: on condition that you cross the Great Sea on your feet,"
if the condition was fulfilled – it is a bill of divorce,
if the condition was not fulfilled – it is not a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתַּעֲלִי לָרָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the חכמים's view stated in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The חכמים's view that an impossible condition is still valid.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a גט given on impossible conditions, which says it is a גט only if the condition is fulfilled.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן תימא says an impossible condition is ignored
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה בן תימא says the גט is valid right away, because a condition that can never be fulfilled is just exaggeration.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן תימא says: A document like this is a valid גט. He gave a general rule: if a condition can never be fulfilled, even though the man set it from the start, he is only exaggerating, and the גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 18 continues and gives the other side of the argument: רבי יהודה בן תימא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the גט waits for the impossible condition to happen, so it never takes effect. רבי יהודה בן תימא says nobody seriously sets a condition that can never happen. So we ignore the condition and the גט works now. This confirms רב's claim in step 17 that the rule 'only a possible condition counts' is רבי יהודה בן תימא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who is just exaggerating, not serious

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה בן תימא cancels the גט because of the impossible condition. He does the opposite: he cancels the condition, and the גט stands.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima says:
Such a document is a valid bill of divorce.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima stated a general rule:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לְקַיְּימוֹ בְּסוֹפוֹ,
phrases.english: Any condition that can never be fulfilled in the end,
even though he set it as a condition from the start,
he is only exaggerating, and the document is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא אוֹמֵר: כָּזֶה – גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 18 by giving the opposing view.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the rule 'only a possible condition counts' belongs to רבי יהודה בן תימא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the ברייתא, where רבי יהודה בן תימא calls an impossible condition mere exaggeration

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know who holds what, the גמרא gives the practical ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, an impossible condition is ignored, and the גט or deal takes effect right away. The view of the חכמים, that the condition still counts, is not followed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for any impossible condition attached to a גט or other legal act.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman says that Rav says:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules between the two views laid out in steps 18–19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An impossible condition is ignored, and the act takes effect right away.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports רבי יהודה בן תימא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the משנה says a possible condition stands, which implies that an impossible one is void. That fits רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Our משנה's wording also shows this. It teaches that any condition he can fulfill in the end, which he set from the start, stands. This implies that if he cannot fulfill it, the condition is void. The גמרא concludes: learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the ruling by reading the משנה's words closely, and then accepts the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits its rule to conditions 'that can be fulfilled.' That limit only makes sense if impossible conditions are treated differently, meaning they are void. That is exactly רבי יהודה בן תימא's view, so the unnamed משנה follows him. This supports ruling like him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise, and its wording proves the point
Learn from this, meaning the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: An impossible condition is void, and the act stands. רב rules this way, and the משנה's wording supports it.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
The mishna is also precise in this way,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה quoted back in step 17.

phrases.english: as it teaches:
any condition that he can fulfill in the end
and he set it as a condition from the start —
his condition stands.
This implies that if he cannot fulfill it,
his condition is void.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the ruling in step 20 with a close reading of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה, and the unnamed משנה, follow רבי יהודה בן תימא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's limiting wording 'that can be fulfilled,' which implies an impossible condition is void

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter השוכר את הפועלים
steps.stepSummary: The chapter השוכר את הפועלים ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, השוכר את הפועלים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line that closes a chapter. No new argument is made here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks the end of the seventh chapter of בבא מציעא. The next line starts a new chapter with a new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the formula said when finishing a chapter
The name of the chapter just finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, Ha-Socher Et Ha-Poalim.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַפּוֹעֲלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last discussion ended in step 21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק השוכר את הפועלים.

steps.title: A borrower who also has the owner working with him is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A new chapter opens. If someone borrows a cow and also borrows or hires its owner at the same time or earlier, he does not pay if the cow dies, based on the פסוק 'אם בעליו עמו לא ישלם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone borrowed a cow and also borrowed the owner's services with it, or hired the owner with it. Or he borrowed or hired the owner first and only afterward borrowed the cow. If the cow died, he is exempt, as it says: 'If its owner is with him, he does not pay.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter, פרק השואל את הפרה, begins with a משנה about the rule called שאלה בבעלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שואל pays even if the animal dies through no fault of his own. The תורה makes an exception when the owner is working for the borrower. The משנה says this exception applies if the owner was taken on together with the cow or before it.

keyTerms.meaning: Borrowed the owner's services, meaning the owner works for him for free

steps.confusionAlert: Borrowing the owner does not mean the owner just happened to be around. It means the owner was actually working for the borrower.
steps.whyThisMatters: This exception, called שאלה בבעלים, is the core topic of the whole new chapter.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who borrowed a cow
and borrowed its owner along with it,
phrases.notes: He means the owner agreed to work for him as a favor, for free.

phrases.english: or hired its owner along with it,
or he borrowed the owner or hired him
and afterward borrowed the cow,
and it died, he is exempt,
as it is stated:
“If its owner is with him, he does not pay.”

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַשּׁוֹאֵל אֶת הַפָּרָה וְשָׁאַל בְּעָלֶיהָ עִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a brand-new chapter after the הדרן in step 22. It is not connected to the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower whose borrowing or hiring of the owner came with or before the borrowing of the cow is exempt if the cow dies.
